rawFindings.title: Missing line guard now breaks bare source-map lookups on malformed trace tokens
rawFindings.explanation: Removing the `line` check causes `originalPositionFor` to run for matched URLs that do not actually include a line number. In that case `line` is parsed as `0`, and traces such as `at http://localhost:9876/base/app.js` are now source-mapped instead of being left as a plain path. This can turn an otherwise readable stack frame into `app.js:0 <- ...` or trigger a lookup failure for maps that do not resolve line 0.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the `line` presence check before using the source map, or explicitly skip mapping when no line number is present.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Given a stack trace line `at http://localhost:9876/base/app.js`, the formatter now calls `originalPositionFor({line: 0, column: 0, ...})` and can emit an incorrect mapped frame instead of `at /some/base/app.js`.
